page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7t.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server instance built on KVM hypervisor architecture. Powered by a dedicated 32-core Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.7 GHz with hyperthreading enabled for 64 vCPUs, it pairs compute capacity with 256 GB of system memory, providing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The host includes 32 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No local NVMe storage is bundled with this instance type, requiring external network-attached block storage for persistent data requirements.

Performance benchmarks demonstrate average single-core capacity coupled with strong multi-core scalability across concurrent operations. Synthetic testing records strong multi-core scores in stress-ng (62,175.76) and Geekbench (16,473.0). Parallelized computational tasks show high throughput, evidenced by Geekbench software compilation with Clang (41,379.0), ray tracing (59,444.0), and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression (286.21 GB/sec). Hardware instruction extensions including AES, VAES, and AVX-512 VNNI support strong cryptography scores in PassMark CPU tests (50,724.75) and efficient prompt processing for small 135M parameter LLMs (2,383.13 tokens/sec).

The hardware configuration provides qualitative cost efficiency by offering high compute core density without requiring specialized GPU accelerators. While single-threaded performance and memory bandwidth benchmark results remain within average ranges, the instance handles concurrent enterprise applications, high-throughput web serving, software build pipelines, and relational database management effectively.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7t.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by a 32-core Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz, delivering 64 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading and 256 GB of memory (4.0 GB per core). Operating on the KVM hypervisor, it features 32 Gbps baseline network throughput without bundled local storage. Benchmarks highlight strong multi-core capabilities, including high PassMark CPU (55,256.18) and PassMark database operation scores (24,723.45), along with accelerated software compilation and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression rates. Cryptographic workloads benefit from hardware vector and AES extensions, while small-model LLM prompt processing reaches 2,383.13 tokens/second. Although single-core scores and memory bandwidth fall into average tiers, the instance's high core count and 1:4 memory allocation offer balanced density and cost efficiency for concurrent enterprise web applications, CI/CD compilation pipelines, relational database clusters, and multi-threaded backend processing tasks.
